newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nestle continues to drive Nigerian stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Nestle continues to drive Nigerian stocks higher.

text.p: Food and beverages market leader Nestle Foods Plc boosted Nigerian stock trading on Tuesday for the second day running as the market absorbed its corporate report including a large dividend, dealers said.
The all-share index rose to 8,721.55 from 8,707.73 on Monday.
"Nestle's dividend of six naira per share surpasses what any other company has so far declared this year and the market is still savouring the result," said one trader.
Nestle's results, announced on Monday, showed after-tax profit for the year ended December 1996 doubled to 1.2 billion naira from 612.8 million in 1995.
The company's share price was up four percent or 2.87 naira on Tuesday after a rise of five percent or 3.53 naira on Monday.
Nestle now dwarfs its main competitor Cadbury Nigeria Plc, whose shares stood at 38.20 on Tuesday.
Nestle is now also the highest-priced stock on the Nigerian bourse, overtaking oil marketer Unipetrol which slumped by 50 kobo on Tuesday to 71.50 naira because of a glut of its shares.

"The market is not happy with Unipetrol because no board has been constituted for it since March last year when government dissolved its board," said one broker. The federal military government holds the majority stake in Unipetrol.
Most other oil products marketing firms, traditionally the toast of the Nigerian bourse, made modest gains on Tuesday.
Among these were Texaco and Mobil, which rose 20 kobo apiece to 47.70 naira and 62.20 respectively.
Another major gainer was BOC Gases, formerly Industrial Gas Plc, which rose 30 kobo to 12.50 naira.
Apart from Unipetrol, the main other loser were Union Bank, which fell by 20 kobo to 16.00 naira, and stationery supplier Thomas Wyatt which fell 15 kobo to 4.25.
